chronicle:
The chill clings to everything here, a dampness that seeps into your bones and settles there. I carried a load of wood earlier, and Flora, my husky, practically vibrated with enthusiasm, pressing against my leg, wanting a scratch. It’s… comforting, having something like her around. A small warmth in this endless expanse of white. 

I spent a little while going over the inventory, just to make sure everything was accounted for. It’s a habit. A compulsion, maybe. The charge rifle felt familiar in my hands; I always prefer to be prepared. The work on the walls and door was slow, each placement deliberate. I briefly dismantled a wall, a moment of frustrated inefficiency, before correcting myself. 

The afternoon bled into a sky of muted gray. I stood and watched it for a while. It's not like the swirling nebulae I used to see through the viewport of a mining vessel, but it’s something. An expanse, at least.

I went hunting. Needed some meat, and there were signs of ibex nearby. Managed to bring down a doe. A clean shot, I suppose, but still… there’s a hollowness that comes with it. The metallic tang of blood hangs in the air, even with the wind. I pursued a ram later, the chase long and arduous. I couldn't bring myself to face it. I had to flee, to hide. It felt...shameful.

Tonight, the stove needed refueling. A simple task, but necessary. A constant cycle of work and survival. This land… it demands everything.
story_bits: Adrian killed an ibex doe with a charge rifle, resulting in gunshot wounds to the neck, right ear, and body.

chronicle:
The chill bites deeper here than any asteroid I've ever mined. It seeps into your bones, a constant reminder of the unforgiving landscape. Today was a flurry of routine, punctuated by moments that left a lingering unease. I spent the morning building a steel shelf – something to keep things organized, a small measure of control in this chaotic place. It feels good to build, to create order. Then the hauling started; sandstone, ibex meat, some plainleather, wood, and those survival meals I’m trying to ration. Flora, bless her, nuzzled my leg during all the commotion. A small comfort in a world that demands so much. 

Around midday, something shifted. A flash of movement, a guttural growl… then a struggle. A wolverine – a snarling, vicious thing – fell before it could do serious harm, though I’m not sure what brought it on. It died soon after. I feel… regret. They’re part of this place, wild and untamed, and I took one from it. A little later, while hauling, I stumbled upon something else entirely. Half-buried in the tundra, a monolith. Ancient, weathered, a silent sentinel from a time long gone. It hummed with a strange energy, a weight of history I couldn't quite place. 

The afternoon bled into the long hours of twilight, filled with the familiar rhythm of harvesting and sowing. Grass, potatoes, rice – the cycle of life and death plays out relentlessly. I cut down trees, birch and pine, then sowed rice again, a futile attempt to tame this land. Every harvest feels like a victory, a small defiance against the elements. The repetition is… grounding. Tonight, the cold settles deeper than before, and the monolith's silent gaze lingers at the edge of my thoughts.
story_bits: A wolverine was killed during a brief encounter.
An ancient monolith was discovered, partially buried in the tundra.

chronicle: The day felt colder than most. A raw, biting wind swept across the tundra as I finished reinforcing the wall – steel this time, a significant expenditure but worth the security. Flora, my husky, was restless, her ears twitching, sensing the unease in the air. I spent a good portion of the morning hauling sandstone and meat, the routine a small comfort against the prickling feeling of being watched. Then came the grizzly. It seemed enraged, circling and snarling, a grim reminder of a previous encounter – a foolish attempt to harvest its carcass that left me bruised and shaken. I took it down with the charge rifle, the energy blast echoing across the landscape. It was quick, merciful, I thought, though the stench lingered. Later, it attacked again, and I had to put it down once more, this time sustaining some scratches – nothing serious, though the stinging on my shoulder and torso is a constant reminder. A brief panic seized me; a moment of weakness when I simply cowered. I hunted it down at last, the grim finality of the gunshot echoing as it fell. Its death, the records will state, was final. A dromedary knight, calling himself Humps, arrived later. A strange sight, this armor on the frozen plains. The day ended with a simple meal at the stove and a moment of quiet meditation. Flora brushed against my leg, a small comfort, and I found myself strangely grateful for her uncomplicated affection.
story_bits: A grizzly bear attacked the colony, resulting in Adrian sustaining scratches to his left shoulder and torso before he was able to kill it.
A visitor, Humps, a dromedary knight from the Tribe of Enbiar, arrived at the colony.
Adrian killed a grizzly bear after it repeatedly attacked the colony.

chronicle:
The day started like any other, with a handful of tasteless rations and the ever-present chill that seemed to seep into the bones despite the meager fire. Hauling supplies, tinkering with the stove – the usual rhythm of survival. Thankfully, the scratches from that grizzly a few days ago finally faded, a minor victory in this harsh land. I even managed a bit of hunting, although the ibex population seems stubbornly sparse. 

The afternoon brought a surprise – or rather, a violent interruption. A wild greatwolf, a beast bigger than any I'd seen before, attacked a poor outsider, Humps. The commotion drew me out; the sight of the greatwolf tearing into the man was…unpleasant. It injured him badly before he fell. It was a brutal fight, and there was nothing I could do to help. I dispatched the wolf quickly enough, a clean cut to its throat, but the cost… it's unsettling. He was a knight, from some tribe. I'll never know his story. I spent the rest of the afternoon hauling and repairing damage. The evening was quiet, another meal by the stove, some stitching at the tailor's bench, trying to keep busy. It’s strange, this need to keep *doing* when the quiet feels like it’s pressing down.

I can almost feel the dust of Old Earth clinging to me still, a constant reminder of everything lost. But the weight of it’s lessened somewhat; a hard day’s work can numb the edges of grief, however briefly. Tonight, though, the chill feels deeper, the shadows longer. I can't shake the image of the greatwolf's death throes, or the feeling that I’ve paid a price for this scrap of land.
story_bits: A greatwolf was killed during an attack, inflicting injuries on an outsider named Humps who subsequently died.
An outsider, Humps, a dromedary knight from the Tribe of Enbiar, arrived at the colony yesterday and died today.

chronicle:
The chill still bites, even with the sun trying to peek through the overcast. It felt good to get back to the mining face this morning after yesterday’s… unpleasantness. Flora, ever the comforting presence, nuzzled against my leg as I ate my simple meal. It’s a small thing, but those moments matter out here. The steel vein is proving rich, denser than anything I’ve encountered before. The clang of my pick against the compacted metal is a strangely satisfying rhythm, a small victory against this barren place. I spent a good portion of the day hacking away at it. 

I managed a stint at the tailor’s bench this morning, patching together a parka from what scraps I could find. The finished product isn’t pretty, no doubt, but it’ll offer some protection from the wind. Hauling the sandstone to the shelf alongside the other supplies felt like a worthwhile addition to our dwindling stores. Later, I noticed a grime of blood on my hands, lingering from a scrape I hadn't registered earlier. A quick clean-up and a plunge into the water cleared it, momentarily chasing away the creeping discomfort. That water is cold, shockingly so, but it’s bracing. Afterwards, I even noticed Nobu had changed affiliations, joining the New Arrivals colony - a rather odd development. Just another strange thing to catalogue in this place. I just hope we can find a way to make a genuinely decent bedroom out of here. It’s so…ugly.
story_bits: A hare was tamed and designated Hare 1.
Adrian constructed a patchleather parka.
Nobu joined the New Arrivals faction.

chronicle:
The air still feels thick with the scent of burnt metal and something else… acrid. It was a chaotic night. Those Toxin Band scum came at us like flies, and one of them, a woman named Engie, was particularly eager to cause trouble. She tried to set a heater ablaze, then went for a steel wall – as if *that* would be an effective tactic. I managed to wound her with the charge rifle, sending several bolts straight in. Heard she passed away this morning. A waste. At least she won’t be bothering us anymore. 

Today was mostly routine, I suppose. Spent a good chunk of the morning preparing food, working at the stove – got to keep the stores full. Then back to the mining, hauling compacted steel. It’s backbreaking work, but the vein I'm working is proving quite rich. A wood-fired generator and a wall lamp are also underway. Needed to refuel the generator too, of course. It feels good to accomplish something, however small. There's always something to build, something to improve. 

Engie, bless her heart, tried to attack me again last night. More static attacks, though thankfully minor. I managed to strip her, extinguish the fires she'd started, and she seemed to suffer some blood loss. She’s gone now, so I don’t have to worry about her shenanigans. 

Flora gave me a quick head-butt this afternoon, a rare show of affection. It almost makes the endless digging worthwhile. Then there were Nikro and Dixon, having a conversation about recreation. Some of them seem to think having fun is important. I suppose it is, in its own way. 

Later, a caravan of slavers from Ralia showed up. Just hung around for a while before leaving. Another reminder of the dangers out there, and the value of what I’m building here.
story_bits: A raider, Engie, attempted to ignite a heater and a steel wall during a raid.
Adrian killed raider Engie with a charge rifle, inflicting gunshot injuries.
A caravan of slavers from Ralia briefly visited the colony.

chronicle:
The wind hasn’t let up, a constant whine across the tundra. It’s a fitting soundtrack, I suppose, for this existence. Mostly, I’ve been at the compacted steel veins today – the repetitive clang of pick against metal is a dull comfort. I managed to get a decent amount down, enough to start a new floor in my room. It’s getting cramped, and I need a little more space to...organize things. 

There were conversations happening around the camp at midday – Hans and Tulyr talking about some pointless game, Mal and Yttryshuk discussing spaceships, which seemed odd given her outlook. Honestly, it's strange how she views the world. I don’t often offer advice, but I felt compelled to tell her to be cautious – there’s a… heaviness around her, a shadow that attracts trouble.  

I spent the afternoon back at the steel, occasionally gathering wood when I could. It's a simple trade, wood for steel, though Hans seemed particularly eager to bargain today. It's strange, watching those Ralia people. They move like they're always being watched, always waiting for something. It makes me uneasy.

Something shifted with Yttryshuk. Suddenly, she’s a slave. The New Arrivals faction. It's a formality, I suppose, but a necessary one. Told her to keep her head down. The easiest way to survive is to be invisible. She didn't look at me when I spoke, just stared at the ground. Flora nuzzled her briefly, a small kindness in all this. 

Several of them – Nikro, Mal, Redfields – have been shadowing Hans. A pack, circling him. I don't know what he's up to, but it feels like it's leading somewhere. Finally managed to trade with Hans, secured some extra wood. Sometimes it's all about getting what you need, regardless of how it feels.  The constant movement, the watchful eyes… I’m starting to feel it, a tightening in my chest. This place… it’s not going to be easy.
story_bits: Yttryshuk was designated as a slave within the New Arrivals faction.
Adrian traded with Hans for wood.

chronicle:
The day started like many others – a packaged survival meal to kick things off, followed by hauling wood. It’s a repetitive task, but the smell of fresh-cut timber is… grounding, I suppose. Flora gave me a nudge against my leg while I was working on the wood floor, a brief, welcome moment of warmth against this endless chill. Later, Yttryshuk joined me in the wood-hauling, and we managed a few conversations. He’s… a difficult colonist. I tried to explain to him the importance of following instructions, hinting at the consequences of disobedience. He seemed to hear me, but I’m not sure he truly understands. His thoughts wander, often landing on dark places. 

I spent the afternoon trying to make the bedroom a little less depressing – a wooden bed and a wall lamp seemed like a start. Meditation helped, although the constant hum of the colony’s machinery tends to intrude. The psychic soothe was a welcome break from the usual anxieties; a rare moment of genuine contentment spread through me. 

Evenings with Yttryshuk are… strange. We spoke about poker, of all things, and oddly enough, comfortable furniture. It's like he's yearning for a life he'll never have. He reminisced about fighting okapis, something I can’t even begin to comprehend, and then drifted into a wistful longing for vacations. It’s unsettling, hearing those desires from someone who seems so resigned. I harvested some rice after midnight, then planted more, knowing the cycle must continue. Each sprout, each harvest, is a small victory against the harshness of this place.
story_bits: Adrian and Yttryshuk engaged in multiple conversations, discussing various topics including hostile beggars and learning blackjack.
Adrian worked on constructing a wooden bed and a wall lamp to improve the colony’s living conditions.
Adrian harvested and sowed rice plants to maintain the colony's food supply.

chronicle:
The chill clings deeper than the frost today, a persistent dampness that settles in the bones. I spent the early hours wrestling with the wood-fired generator again – it feels like a constant battle against the elements and the inefficiency of the thing. At least it keeps the stove going, which means I could get some food prepared. 

Mostly, the day revolved around Yttryshuk. She’s… a curious presence. She moves with a sort of weary grace as she tends the rice, harvesting and replanting with a quiet diligence. Our conversations are peculiar; cedars, sweating, pumpkins – random tangents that bounce off each other. It’s almost…companionable, in a detached sort of way. I try to be amiable, I truly do. But there's a tension there, a knowledge that her position as a slave necessitates a certain…management. I can't afford any disruption. I warned her, softly, about disobedience. Some things are best left unsaid, yet must be known. Her waiting afterward felt unsettling.

The brief attempt to suppress her felt… necessary. It’s not a pleasant task, but stability demands a certain level of control. It's a burden, really. The growling in my gut isn't just hunger; it's the weight of responsibility. The glimpse of a rotting corpse earlier – a grim reminder of what can happen when things unravel. It stirs a feeling in me, a sense of needing to hoard, to protect, to control. Not just resources, but order itself. 

Later, more rice, more fuel for the generator, more food. It’s a rhythm, a constant cycle of work and provision. This colony… it's fragile. It needs to be strong. I need to be strong.
story_bits: Adrian and Yttryshuk engaged in several conversations throughout the day, discussing varied topics.
Adrian attempted to suppress Yttryshuk, indicating an ongoing effort to maintain control over the slave.

chronicle:
The feeling started subtly, a prickling unease as I neared the ancient wall earlier this evening. I can’t say what it was, something about the stones themselves… foreboding, perhaps. I spent most of the afternoon mining compacted steel, the repetitive clang of the pickaxe strangely comforting against the creeping anxiety. A few moments staring at the sky helped, too.  It’s a bleak canvas out here, but the stars… they’re something. A little pemmican kept the hunger at bay. 

Later, I started deconstructing that granite wall – a tedious job, but necessary.  The day suddenly dissolved into chaos.  I was just trying to pry a block loose when the yelling started. Then... the *things*. Dark, twisted shapes – spikes and limbs flailing in the dim light. I ran, instinctively. Fled. I don’t relish cowardice, but survival has always been the priority.  I fired a few shots, but it felt like spitting at a storm.

Combat.  It was… desperate.  Yttryshuk fought alongside me, a grim and silent figure.  We managed to bring down one of them, but they kept coming. The charge rifle roared, each pulse a fleeting moment of hope.  My fists connected with another, a sickening thud.  Then, the pain.  A wave of it, crashing over me. A cracked femur, the sting of stabs...  I was down. 

Now, I lie here on a rough bed, the world blurring at the edges. The pain is… significant. Yttryshuk tried to stop the blood loss, but there's not much she can do. I can hear the sounds of ongoing fighting – Flora barking, Yttryshuk shouting. Everything feels distant, unreal. Just… exhaustion.  I hope I wake up.
story_bits: A group of hostile entities attacked the colony, resulting in significant injuries to Adrian and Yttryshuk.
Yttryshuk and Adrian downed an enemy, resulting in gunshot and fist injuries.
An ancient granite wall was partially deconstructed.
